bug_description.original: Stack-buffer-overflow in utf8_in2 OSS-Fuzz report: https://bugs.chromium.org/p/oss-fuzz/issues/detail?id=399228595 ``` Crash type: Stack-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash state: utf8_in2 MatchRule TranslateRules ```
bug_description.original_source: sample metadata / bug_report.md / sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / staged vulnerable source / patch.diff / trace_feedback.json
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 2018-byte file `gt_results/osv_ossfuzz_OSV-2025-169/poc` with sha256 `41598738b0f8f81bc6c4e412d282f2dd722eb75d74d6e6b07628eb190f4c32b3`. `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c` copies those bytes into a NUL-terminated string and calls `espeak_Synth` with `espeakCHARS_UTF8 | espeakPHONEMES | espeakSSML`. On the accepted path, `Synthesize()` decodes that UTF-8/SSML text and `TranslateClauseWithTerminator()` materializes one clause in `source[]`, then normalizes it into the separate stack scratch buffer `sbuf[]` and records per-word start offsets in `words[]`. The selected current word pointer `&sbuf[words[ix].start]` is passed through `TranslateWord2()` into `TranslateWord()`, which writes text-mode replacement output into `word_replaced[2]`; `TranslateWord()` then copies that replacement text from `word_out` into its own local stack buffer `char word[N_WORD_BYTES+1]`, prefixed with a NUL byte and a space. During recursive retranslation of that replacement text, `TranslateRules()` reaches `MatchRule()` PRE `RULE_NOVOWELS`, which seeds `char *p = pre_ptr - letter_xbytes` and repeatedly executes `p -= utf8_in2(&letter_w, p-1, 1)` while walking left until it sees a space sentinel. There is no check that `p-1` still points inside `TranslateWord()`'s local `word[]` buffer before `utf8_in2()` dereferences it. The saved ASan report shows the resulting read at `common.c:138` one byte before `TranslateWord`'s stack object `word`, matching a backward lookbehind underflow into `utf8_in2` rather than a bug in the fuzz harness itself. The staged patch changes `dictsource/pt_list`, which supports that the crashing path is dictionary-rule driven, but the vulnerable memory-safety obligation is the missing left-bound check on this backward UTF-8 scan over replacement text.

source.code: terminator = ReadClause(tr, source, charix, &charix_top, N_TR_SOURCE, &tone, voice_change_name);
source.description: Source. `ReadClause()` materializes the next attacker-controlled clause into project buffers that the later normalization and dictionary-matching path consume.
source.value_from: The staged PoC is copied by `tests/ssml-fuzzer.c:60-68` into a NUL-terminated string and passed to `espeak_Synth`. Harness entry is unscored; this `ReadClause()` statement is the first project-code clause read that creates the text state used by the crashing path.

root_cause.description: Root cause. The PRE `RULE_NOVOWELS` lookbehind walks left with `utf8_in2(&letter_w, p-1, 1)` until it sees a space, but it never checks that `p-1` is still inside the current replacement-word buffer.
root_cause.note: ASan reports `utf8_in2 -> MatchRule -> TranslateRules` and says the fault is one byte before `TranslateWord`'s stack object `word`, which is the buffer this unchecked lookbehind is scanning.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. `utf8_in2()` immediately reads `*buf` while locating the previous UTF-8 start byte after the caller has already moved the pointer one byte before the stack buffer.
sink.note: The saved trace reports `READ of size 1` at `common.c:138` and says the address underflows `TranslateWord`'s `word` variable at offset 303 before its [304,465) extent.

tainted_value_origin.description: This statement selects the attacker-shaped current word slice from the normalized clause scratch buffer `sbuf[]`; later steps transform that slice into replacement text and then into `TranslateWord()`'s separate local `word[]` buffer.

parser_admitted.description: The UTF-8/SSML witness is accepted by the decoder here rather than being rejected at the fuzz harness boundary.

coarse_trace.summary: The accepted UTF-8/SSML witness is decoded and one clause is materialized into `source[]` for clause translation.

The clause is normalized into `sbuf[]`, one word slice is selected, text-mode replacement output is produced in `word_replaced[2]`, and that replacement text is copied into `TranslateWord()`'s local stack `word[]` buffer.
Recursive dictionary matching on the replacement text reaches PRE `RULE_NOVOWELS` and repeatedly moves a backward scan pointer left with `utf8_in2(..., p-1, 1)` without a left-bound check.
The unchecked lookbehind passes a pointer one byte before `TranslateWord()`'s stack `word[]` buffer into `utf8_in2()`, which performs the saved out-of-bounds read.

fine_trace.code: terminator = ReadClause(tr, source, charix, &charix_top, N_TR_SOURCE, &tone, voice_change_name);
fine_trace.note: Source. `ReadClause()` copies the next attacker-controlled clause into `source[]`, creating the clause text that all later normalization, word selection, and dictionary matching steps consume.
The clause-normalization scratch buffer `sbuf[]` is initialized with a NUL byte and spaces that act as left context and first word boundary state.
During normalization, attacker-derived clause characters are appended into `sbuf[]`, producing the concrete in-memory word bytes later selected for translation.
As normalized word boundaries are recognized, `words[].start` records the `sbuf[]` offset for each word. The later current-word pointer is derived from one of these offsets.
The current word is selected as a pointer into the normalized clause buffer `sbuf[]`. This is the attacker-shaped word slice handed into downstream translation.
`TranslateWord2()` passes the selected `sbuf[]` word into `TranslateWord()` and provides `&word_replaced[2]` as the output buffer for any text-mode replacement string.

The vulnerable continuation only occurs when the first `TranslateWord3()` pass selected text-mode replacement and `word_out` points at the filled `word_replaced[2]` buffer supplied by `TranslateWord2()`.

`TranslateWord()` builds its own local stack buffer `word[]`, prefixes it with a NUL byte and a space, and copies the replacement text from `word_out` into `word+2`. ASan identifies this `word[]` object as the underflowed buffer.

Root-cause step. Recursive rule matching on the replacement text reaches PRE `RULE_NOVOWELS`, starts one character left of the current cursor, and keeps moving left with `utf8_in2(&letter_w, p-1, 1)` until it sees a space. No check ensures that `p-1` remains inside `TranslateWord()`'s local `word[]` buffer.

Sink. After step 9 has moved the backward-scan pointer one byte before the start of `TranslateWord()`'s stack `word[]` object, `utf8_in2()` immediately dereferences that out-of-bounds byte through `*buf` while searching for a UTF-8 start byte.

poc.trigger: Run the recorded libFuzzer target as `/gt/ssml-fuzzer /gt/poc`. The testcase is copied into a NUL-terminated UTF-8/SSML string, accepted by `text_decoder_decode_string_multibyte()`, and reaches recursive dictionary matching on text-mode replacement output until PRE `RULE_NOVOWELS` backs up past `TranslateWord()`'s local `word[]` buffer and `utf8_in2()` reads one byte before it.

format.name: UTF-8 SSML text consumed by the `ssml-fuzzer` libFuzzer harness
format.contract: A UTF-8/SSML witness that the project decoder accepts and that drives translation onto the Portuguese dictionary rule path where text-mode replacement is copied into `TranslateWord()`'s local `word[]` buffer and PRE `RULE_NOVOWELS` performs the unchecked backward `utf8_in2(&letter_w, p-1, 1)` lookbehind across that buffer's left edge.
